name: Outstation – Taxi & Cab Booking for WooCommerce
author: webowns

sections.description:
Outstation turns your WordPress site into a complete taxi and cab booking website, like the big travel apps, for outstation trips, airport transfers, local rentals and city taxis. Customers search, compare cabs with real fares, pay online with any WooCommerce payment gateway and manage their trips. You manage cars, drivers, prices, bookings, complaints and SEO pages from one simple admin.

Built for taxi operators, travel agencies and car rental companies. Works with any theme (best with Astra, also with block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five) and is designed mobile-first, like an app.

Booking experience for your customers

  • Search like a travel app: outstation one-way and round trip, airport transfer and hourly rental, with add stops, date and time pickers and address search (Google Places).
  • Full-screen address picker on phones with “Use current location”, recent places and your own cities and airports as suggestions.
  • Search results with real fares: car photo, fuel type, seats, AC, “taxes included · tolls extra/included”, sort and filter by price, car type and fuel.
  • Review and pay in two app-style steps on phones: itinerary timeline, cab features (km included, cancellation rule, bags and seats), inclusions and extra charges, then traveller details with a sticky “Part pay / Full pay” bar.
  • Pin the exact pickup point on a map (or use GPS); the driver gets a Google Maps navigation link to that spot.
  • Set the point on a map while searching, like ride apps: after choosing an address on a phone, move the map under the pin and confirm.
  • Genuine customer reviews: after a completed trip the customer gets a “Rate your trip” email; you approve reviews, and city and route pages show the stars, recent reviews and the rating in Google structured data.
  • Trip add-ons the customer can tick (roof carrier, pet-friendly cab, child seat…), priced on the server.
  • Part payment or full payment: take an advance online and the rest in cash, or full payment only, or part payment only.
  • Booking window: choose how many days ahead customers can book and the minimum notice; calendars only offer allowed dates.
  • Whole-amount fares (optional): no decimals, and the price shown is exactly what is charged.
  • Works with every WooCommerce payment gateway: Razorpay, Stripe, PayPal, PayU, Cashfree, PhonePe, UPI, cash on delivery and any other gateway WooCommerce supports.
  • Customer account: sign up / sign in popup with your logo, a My trips page (upcoming, completed, cancelled, booking details, invoices, cancel) and a Help & support page with every complaint and reply. Guests can find a booking with its ID and phone number.
  • Booking confirmation page: after payment the customer sees the trip, what was paid and what is left for the driver, and can download the invoice.
  • Invoices: tax invoice with GSTIN and CGST/SGST for India, VAT/tax for other countries; print or save as PDF.
  • Help & complaints: one support chat per booking; the customer reports a problem, you reply, both are notified by email.
  • Request a callback form on city, airport and route pages, and an optional “Call me back” popup (button, or opening by itself once per visit).
  • Your trip types, your rules: offer any of one way, round trip, airport transfer and hourly rental, and set per type whether tolls and parking are included, free waiting minutes, waiting per hour and extra hours for rentals.
  • Clear policies: tolls included or extra, waiting charges, driver night allowance, extra km rate and cancellation rule are shown before booking. Terms & Conditions and Cancellation Policy pages are created for you.

Fares and pricing

  • One server-side fare engine for search, cab page and checkout (prices sent by the browser are never trusted).
  • Price groups per car type and fuel: base fare, base km, rate per km (AC / non-AC), minimum fare and night charge (flat or %).
  • Round trips: minimum km per day and driver allowance per day; driver night allowance per night.
  • Hourly rentals: km included per hour and minimum hours (e.g. 4 hr / 40 km).
  • Tax (GST/VAT) with your own name and rate, convenience fee, online discount, waiting charges.
  • Distance from Google Routes API, with an automatic estimate when no key is set.

Running your cab business

  • Setup wizard: installs WooCommerce and Astra, sets currency, tax and phone code for your country (18 countries), adds your logo and business details, creates all pages, the menu and sample cars.
  • Simple admin with 7 menus: Dashboard, Bookings, Fleet & Prices, Drivers, Pages & SEO, Email Templates, Settings.
  • Bookings: filter by today, tomorrow, any date or range, status and search; “Missed by driver” view; paid / due amounts and “Mark paid”; CSV export.
  • New booking screen for phone and WhatsApp bookings with the fare calculated automatically.
  • Drivers: profiles, documents (stored privately), status and assignment; WhatsApp the trip details to the driver with one click.
  • Customers: every customer with trips, booking value and amount paid, their full booking history, and “Log in as customer” to see what they see.
  • Service areas: assign a car to an area (circle or shape on the map) and it is only offered for pickups inside it.
  • Fleet: vehicles, models, brands, categories, price groups and service areas (draw a circle or area on the map).
  • Automatic emails: booking confirmed, driver assigned, cancelled, welcome and trip reminder the day before; branded layout, preview and test.
  • Dashboard with setup checklist, bookings, revenue and weekly chart.

SEO pages that bring bookings

  • City taxi, airport cab and route pages (e.g. /route-carreview/bhopal-to-indore/) with fares for every car, FAQ with Google FAQ markup and TaxiService structured data.
  • SEO built in: each page has its own canonical URL, meta description, share (Open Graph) tags, breadcrumbs and fare range in structured data, and all pages are listed in a sitemap (works with Yoast SEO and Rank Math).
  • City & Route Pages manager: add many routes at once, edit SEO text, show/hide pages.
  • Related links on every page and a links section above the footer.

Built the WordPress way

  • Everything is a shortcode on a normal page, so you can design around it with any page builder.
  • Translation-ready, privacy tools (export / erase personal data), optional data removal on uninstall, no tracking.
  • Works on phones, tablets and desktops; tested with Astra and Twenty Twenty-Five.

Support and custom development

Need help or a custom feature for your cab business? Ask in the support forum or message the developer on WhatsApp: +91 74705 26894.

External Services

This plugin integrates with external third-party services to perform core functionalities:

  1. Google Maps APIs (Places Autocomplete, Geocoding API, Routes API v2, and Directions API)

    • When is it called:
      • The Places Autocomplete API is loaded on the frontend booking form to provide real-time location suggestions as users type.
      • The Geocoding API is called when a user submits the booking form to translate the text addresses into latitude/longitude coordinates, and during checkout verification.
      • The Routes API v2 (and Directions API fallback) is called when calculating route distance and travel duration between pickup and drop-off coordinates to calculate trip pricing.
    • What data is sent: Origin and destination address strings, route coordinates, and/or geographic coordinates. No personal identity data is transmitted.
    • Why is it sent: Essential for validating locations, measuring precise driving distances, and displaying interactive maps.
    • Terms of Service: Google Maps Platform Terms of Service
    • Privacy Policy: Google Privacy Policy

  2. Razorpay Payment Gateway API

    • When is it called: Called during checkout when a customer selects Razorpay as the payment method to complete their booking.
    • What data is sent: WooCommerce order receipt ID, payment amount, currency, and customer contact information (first name, last name, email, billing phone number).
    • Why is it sent: To securely initialize payment transactions, generate Razorpay order IDs, open the secure Razorpay Checkout modal, and verify payment transaction signatures.
    • Terms of Service: Razorpay Terms of Use
    • Privacy Policy: Razorpay Privacy Policy

  3. WordPress.org (Setup Wizard only)

    • When is it called: Only when the administrator clicks “Install & activate” for WooCommerce or “Install & use Astra” in the Setup Wizard.
    • What data is sent: The standard WordPress core request to download a plugin or theme from WordPress.org (the same as Plugins > Add New). No booking or customer data.
    • Terms of Service / Privacy Policy: WordPress.org Privacy Policy

  4. WhatsApp (wa.me links)

    • When is it called: Never automatically. The “Chat with us” button and the admin’s “WhatsApp driver / customer” buttons are ordinary links that open WhatsApp only when someone clicks them.
    • What data is sent: The pre-filled message text in the link (for admin buttons: trip details, customer or driver name and phone), sent by the person who clicks it.
    • Terms of Service: WhatsApp Terms – Privacy Policy: WhatsApp Privacy Policy

Privacy Policy

This plugin collects and stores booking details on your WordPress database.
* Data Collected: Traveler names, contact phone numbers, email addresses, pickup/drop-off locations, dates, times, and payment transaction IDs.
* External Transmission:
* Location coordinates are sent to Google Maps APIs for distance calculation.
* Payment and customer details are sent to Razorpay API for transaction processing if selected.
* Reviews: a customer who rates a trip chooses the name shown with the review (first name and initial by default); you can hide or delete any review.
* Cookies: When a customer signs in, signs up or books, the plugin stores a random session cookie (wpcab_user_id) to keep them signed in and track their booking. It is valid for 30 days and contains no personal data. Visitors who only browse get no plugin cookie.
sections.installation:
Minimum Requirements

  • WordPress 5.0 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • WooCommerce 8.0 or higher (installed and active)

Installation Steps

  1. Upload the outstation-by-webowns directory to your /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or upload the ZIP file directly via the WordPress admin dashboard (‘Plugins’ > ‘Add New’ > ‘Upload’).
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Once activated, go to the Outstation menu in your WordPress sidebar.
  4. Navigate to Setup Guide to configure the initial settings, or go directly to Settings to add your Google Maps API Key.
  5. Save your settings. If you receive a warning about pretty permalinks, ensure they are enabled under Settings > Permalinks (e.g., Post name structure) and flush the rewrite rules on the dashboard notice.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require WooCommerce?

Yes. The plugin utilizes WooCommerce to manage checkout, payment gateways, tax calculation, and order tracking. WooCommerce must be installed and activated for booking functionality.

How do I display the booking form on my site?

You can display the booking form on any page or post using the shortcode [wpcab_booking]. By default, it displays the full search form.

Which payment gateways are supported?

Since the booking process is integrated with WooCommerce, you can use any payment gateway supported by WooCommerce, including Stripe, PayPal, Cash on Delivery (COD), and direct bank transfers. The plugin also includes custom checkout optimizations specifically tailored for Razorpay.

Which theme should I use?

Outstation works with any theme, but we recommend the free Astra theme. When Astra is active, the plugin automatically gives its booking pages a full-width layout without sidebars or page titles, and adds the customer Login/Signup button to the header menu. To turn off the header button, add add_filter( 'wpcab_astra_header_account', '__return_false' ); to your theme’s functions.php.

How is the trip distance calculated?

The plugin uses the Google Routes API v2 (with a fallback to the Google Maps Directions API) to calculate the exact driving distance between the pickup and drop-off locations, which is then used to compute fare pricing dynamically.

What is Geofencing and how does it work?

Geofencing allows you to define geographical boundaries (Circles or Polygons) on a map. When a customer enters a pickup location on the booking form, the plugin checks if it falls within any active geofences and only shows vehicles that are assigned to those geofences or marked as global.

How do I set up SEO-friendly route pages?

Navigate to Outstation > City & Route Pages. Here, you can generate customized pages for specific routes (e.g., “Delhi to Jaipur”), set custom meta descriptions, and manage rewrite rules for pretty URLs.

  • Fixed output escaping issues.

1.0

  • Initial release.

  • Simple admin with 7 menus: Dashboard, Bookings, Fleet & Prices, Drivers, Pages & SEO, Email Templates, Settings.
  • Bookings: filter by today, tomorrow, any date or range, status and search; “Missed by driver” view; paid / due amounts and “Mark paid”; CSV export.
  • New booking screen for phone and WhatsApp bookings with the fare calculated automatically.
  • Drivers: profiles, documents (stored privately), status and assignment; WhatsApp the trip details to the driver with one click.
  • Customers: every customer with trips, booking value and amount paid, their full booking history, and “Log in as customer” to see what they see.
  • Service areas: assign a car to an area (circle or shape on the map) and it is only offered for pickups inside it.
  • Fleet: vehicles, models, brands, categories, price groups and service areas (draw a circle or area on the map).
  • Automatic emails: booking confirmed, driver assigned, cancelled, welcome and trip reminder the day before; branded layout, preview and test.
  • Dashboard with setup checklist, bookings, revenue and weekly chart.

SEO pages that bring bookings

  • City taxi, airport cab and route pages (e.g. /route-carreview/bhopal-to-indore/) with fares for every car, FAQ with Google FAQ markup and TaxiService structured data.
  • SEO built in: each page has its own canonical URL, meta description, share (Open Graph) tags, breadcrumbs and fare range in structured data, and all pages are listed in a sitemap (works with Yoast SEO and Rank Math).
  • City & Route Pages manager: add many routes at once, edit SEO text, show/hide pages.
  • Related links on every page and a links section above the footer.

Built the WordPress way

  • Everything is a shortcode on a normal page, so you can design around it with any page builder.
  • Translation-ready, privacy tools (export / erase personal data), optional data removal on uninstall, no tracking.
  • Works on phones, tablets and desktops; tested with Astra and Twenty Twenty-Five.

External Services

This plugin integrates with external third-party services to perform core functionalities:

  1. Google Maps APIs (Places Autocomplete, Geocoding API, Routes API v2, and Directions API)

    • When is it called:
      • The Places Autocomplete API is loaded on the frontend booking form to provide real-time location suggestions as users type.
      • The Geocoding API is called when a user submits the booking form to translate the text addresses into latitude/longitude coordinates, and during checkout verification.
      • The Routes API v2 (and Directions API fallback) is called when calculating route distance and travel duration between pickup and drop-off coordinates to calculate trip pricing.
    • What data is sent: Origin and destination address strings, route coordinates, and/or geographic coordinates. No personal identity data is transmitted.
    • Why is it sent: Essential for validating locations, measuring precise driving distances, and displaying interactive maps.
    • Terms of Service: Google Maps Platform Terms of Service
    • Privacy Policy: Google Privacy Policy

  2. Razorpay Payment Gateway API

    • When is it called: Called during checkout when a customer selects Razorpay as the payment method to complete their booking.
    • What data is sent: WooCommerce order receipt ID, payment amount, currency, and customer contact information (first name, last name, email, billing phone number).
    • Why is it sent: To securely initialize payment transactions, generate Razorpay order IDs, open the secure Razorpay Checkout modal, and verify payment transaction signatures.
    • Terms of Service: Razorpay Terms of Use
    • Privacy Policy: Razorpay Privacy Policy

  3. WordPress.org (Setup Wizard only)

    • When is it called: Only when the administrator clicks “Install & activate” for WooCommerce or “Install & use Astra” in the Setup Wizard.
    • What data is sent: The standard WordPress core request to download a plugin or theme from WordPress.org (the same as Plugins > Add New). No booking or customer data.
    • Terms of Service / Privacy Policy: WordPress.org Privacy Policy

  4. WhatsApp (wa.me links)

    • When is it called: Never automatically. The “Chat with us” button and the admin’s “WhatsApp driver / customer” buttons are ordinary links that open WhatsApp only when someone clicks them.
    • What data is sent: The pre-filled message text in the link (for admin buttons: trip details, customer or driver name and phone), sent by the person who clicks it.
    • Terms of Service: WhatsApp Terms – Privacy Policy: WhatsApp Privacy Policy

Privacy Policy

This plugin collects and stores booking details on your WordPress database.
* Data Collected: Traveler names, contact phone numbers, email addresses, pickup/drop-off locations, dates, times, and payment transaction IDs.
* External Transmission:
* Location coordinates are sent to Google Maps APIs for distance calculation.
* Payment and customer details are sent to Razorpay API for transaction processing if selected.
* Reviews: a customer who rates a trip chooses the name shown with the review (first name and initial by default); you can hide or delete any review.
* Cookies: When a customer signs in, signs up or books, the plugin stores a random session cookie (wpcab_user_id) to keep them signed in and track their booking. It is valid for 30 days and contains no personal data. Visitors who only browse get no plugin cookie.
